problems.givens: Equiconvex lens, index 1.5, focal length 60 cm, one face silvered.
problems.assumptions: Thin lens in unit-index air, with the quoted focal length measured in air. Orient the unsilvered face toward the source.
problems.conditional: Equal radius magnitudes 600 mm. In the zero-thickness limit the returning pencil focuses 150 mm before the pole, equivalent to a concave mirror.

problems.givens: Thin equiconvex lens, index 1.5, equal radius magnitudes 25 cm, one face silvered, real object in front required to coincide with its image.
problems.assumptions: Unit-index air outside. Orient the unsilvered face toward the object.
problems.conditional: The nonzero object distance is 125 mm from the thin element.

syntheticNativeGeometry.scope: Use the left surface of one CircleGlass with centre (R,0) and radius R, and a separate immersed ArcMirror patch of radius R with centre (20-R,0). All lengths in mm. The mirror patch lies strictly inside the glass. The positive separation is synthetic. No touching native surfaces or coincident-element run.

acceptance.negativeControl: With the mirror removed, the ray may transmit across the far side of the circle but must never give a leftward detector crossing.
acceptance.interpretation: Intersect measured return directions with the axis. Exact first-order reference uses refraction, positive translation in glass, spherical reflection, the return translation and exit refraction. Synthetic finite separations have distinct predictions from the thin-source limits.
